hints: Zoom in on the particles as the balloon warms. Are they getting bigger, or doing something else?

Heat makes particles move faster, and their size stays the same. Fast particles hit the balloon's wall harder and more often, so it stretches. Picture kids in a bouncy castle. When they jump harder, the walls bulge, but the kids haven't grown.
Heat it to 90 °C. Then compare the particle size and speed readings with the start.
